headline: Strait Tensions and Semiconductor Surge Color a Split Friday Close
body_html:
Markets finished Friday's session on a divided note, with 286 names in our 549-name universe closing lower against 259 advancers. The commodity complex led the charge: Energy added 1.35% and Materials rose 1.22%, both fuelled by fresh geopolitical anxiety in the Persian Gulf after a tanker attack near the Strait of Hormuz sent crude prices climbing by more than a dollar. Software bore the steepest losses, shedding 1.38%, while Homebuilders and Consumer names also finished in the red.

Semiconductors proved the session's standout bright spot, gaining 1.13% as a group. MaxLinear surged 10.68% to top the leaderboard, followed by Sandisk at 7.39% and AMD at 6.50% — the latter pair riding optimism around a flash-memory outlook that one market observer described as a meaningful positive for the sector. Copart and Alpha Metallurgical Resources each added more than 6%, reflecting strength in autos and metallurgical coal respectively. On the downside, N-able dropped 6.52% and ZoomInfo fell 6.03%, dragging the broader software cohort lower.

Heading into the new week, the dominant macro overhang is Hormuz. Slowing strait traffic, a reported oil slick off Oman, and an unresolved standoff between Washington and Tehran over energy sanctions keep the geopolitical risk premium elevated. Traders will watch crude closely alongside any diplomatic signals, while the semiconductor tape — already energised — may set the tone for growth sentiment as earnings season moves toward its final stretch.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Choke Point Tightens as Tanker Attack Sparks Fresh Alarm
briefs.body: A vessel operated by Abu Dhabi's national oil company came under attack while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, compounding an already fragile shipping environment. Traffic through the waterway has slowed further after Washington threatened additional economic pressure on Tehran. Iran signalled no intention of backing down, and the White House suggested current naval deployments may prove insufficient.

briefs.headline: Crude Ticks Higher on Combined Gulf Threat and Oman Spill Reports
briefs.body: Oil prices rose more than a dollar on Friday as tanker attacks and a lack of diplomatic progress weighed on supply expectations. Separately, two slicks were reported in Gulf waters off Oman, raising the prospect of an environmental disaster that could further disrupt regional shipping lanes heading into the new week.

briefs.headline: MaxLinear and Sandisk Lead a Semiconductor Revival
briefs.body: MaxLinear jumped 10.68% and Sandisk climbed 7.39% on Friday, propelling the Semiconductors sector to a 1.13% gain — among the session's top-performing groups. Upbeat commentary from the flash-memory space earlier in the week appeared to reinvigorate investor appetite across chip-related names, with AMD adding another 6.50% to the sector's tailwind.

briefs.headline: Software Stocks Slide as N-able and ZoomInfo Lead Decliners
briefs.body: The Software sector fell 1.38%, the worst showing of any group on Friday. N-able dropped 6.52% and ZoomInfo shed 6.03%, together accounting for two of the six largest single-stock declines in the universe. GoDaddy and Qualys also retreated sharply, underscoring persistent valuation pressure on recurring-revenue technology names.

briefs.headline: Etna Eruption Disrupts European Air Traffic, Adding to Macro Noise
briefs.body: A fiery eruption of Mount Etna forced the cancellation or diversion of hundreds of flights across the Mediterranean region on Friday. The disruption added another layer of uncertainty for European markets, which were already contending with rising oil prices that snapped a four-week equity rally on the continent.

briefs.headline: Mali Ransom Revelation Adds Geopolitical Dimension to Risk Calculus
briefs.body: A United Nations report concluded that a hostage ransom of fifty million dollars helped bankroll an al Qaeda offensive in Mali, sharpening concerns about militant financing in the Sahel. The finding broadens the geopolitical risk map for global investors beyond the Gulf, potentially affecting sentiment toward frontier-market and commodity-linked assets in the week ahead.
